name: Deep Research: A Systematic Survey (Shi et al.)
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2512.02038 (v1 submitted 24 Nov 2025). Subjects: cs.CL (primary), cs.AI, cs.IR. arXiv-issued DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2512.02038. Not (yet) peer-reviewed at a conference/journal; the authors state it will be continuously updated. A ResearchGate mirror also lists DOI 10.13140/RG.2.2 for the preprint.

code_url: https://github.com/mangopy/Deep-Research-Survey (companion paper-list repository; no method code since this is a survey).
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/mangopy/Deep-Research-Survey (continuously-updated GitHub paper list, ~319 stars / 54 commits, last README update Jan 2026; organizes Deep Research papers by the four key components, training paradigms, and benchmarks/resources).
task_domain: Survey of Deep Research (DR) systems: LLM agents that combine reasoning with external tools (search engines, web browsing, code execution) to solve complex, open-ended research tasks. Surveyed task families span agentic information seeking (open-domain QA, multi-hop QA, live web navigation), integrated/comprehensive report generation (survey/long-form report/poster/slides generation), AI-for-research (idea generation, experimental execution, academic writing, peer review), and software engineering. Spans QA, web, tool-use, decision-making, and long-form generation domains.
problem_setting: A comprehensive literature review (not a method). It formalizes DR as a closed-loop, interactive, single- or multi-agent workflow that takes a complex research question and produces a structured, citation-grounded long-form answer (e.g., a report). The setting is predominantly online/interactive (live web, tools, APIs, code executors), long-horizon, and multi-turn, with minimal human supervision; it contrasts this with offline static-corpus RAG. Supervision spans training-free workflow prompting, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) cold-start, and end-to-end agentic reinforcement learning (RL). The survey introduces a three-stage capability roadmap (Phase I Agentic Search; Phase II Integrated Research; Phase III Full-stack AI Scientist) and four foundational components (query planning, information acquisition, memory management, answer generation).
what_is_retrieved: Predominantly documents/web pages/evidence acquired via search engines, web browsing, tools, APIs, and local files, plus multimodal content (tables, charts, figures with grounded pointers for citation). The survey also surveys memory retrieval: consolidated experiences/episodic memories, structured graphs/knowledge bases, skills (skill libraries), workflows/procedural memory, and user profiles/preferences. So the retrieved units span docs, tools/API calls, structured graph entities, and stored experiences/memories rather than only static text.
retrieval_grounding: HYBRID. The dominant DR grounding surveyed is interaction with a DYNAMIC external world (live commercial web search like Google/Bing, web APIs, tools, code executors) rather than a frozen pre-indexed corpus, which the survey explicitly cites as the key limitation of standard RAG ('static retrieval loop, relying solely on pre-indexed corpora'). It also surveys a GROWING/episodic agent memory (memory management component: consolidation, indexing, updating, forgetting) that the agent writes during deployment, plus classic static-corpus lexical/dense retrieval. Overall grounding is hybrid: real-time external tools/web + growing agent memory + static corpora.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Mixed across the surveyed spectrum. Classic information-filtering still uses fixed top-k document selection by relevance. But the survey emphasizes a shift toward completeness-driven objectives for DR: WideSearch is highlighted as requiring agents to 'thoroughly and accurately acquire all large-scale atomic information that meets a set of criteria' (set completeness), and report-generation evaluation uses key-point coverage / recall. Adaptive retrieval reframes the objective as variable, precision/cost-driven (retrieve only when knowledge is insufficient) rather than a fixed top-k. So both fixed top-k ranking and completeness/coverage objectives are surveyed, with DR pushing toward completeness and coverage.
retrieval_unit: Surveyed as a spectrum. Information-acquisition units: document/passage/chunk (lexical BM25/TF-IDF, dense, commercial web search), multimodal units (text-with-layout, figures/chart thumbnails via CLIP/SigLIP/BLIP, parsed table cells/chart data marks with grounded pointers), and tool/API calls. Memory units: consolidated summaries/event logs, structured graph entities/triples/sub-graphs (knowledge graphs), tree nodes (MemTree), skills (skill library), procedural workflows, and timestamped episodic memories. Query-planning units: sub-queries/sub-tasks. So units range from token/snippet and document to KG-subgraph, tool-API, skill, workflow, and case/experience.
index_source: Hybrid. Static corpora (Wikipedia, local resources for BM25/dense retrieval) coexist with live external sources (commercial web search APIs, web pages, tools) accessed at test time, and with a growing agent memory built online via consolidation/indexing/updating/forgetting. The survey explicitly distinguishes DR's dynamic, online-induced, real-world information access from RAG's offline-frozen pre-indexed corpus. Memory indexing uses LSH/HNSW/FAISS, signal-enhanced (temporal+semantic metadata), graph-based (HippoRAG, A-Mem), and timeline-based (Theanine, Zep bi-temporal) structures built over consolidated experiences.
index_structure_topology: Surveyed across all topologies. Retrieval indices: flat vector / inverted-index (BM25, dense ANN via FAISS/HNSW), reciprocal-rank-fusion over multimodal indices. Memory indices: (i) signal-enhanced (metadata: temporal, topic, keyword, emotional context pivots; LongMemEval, MMS); (ii) graph-based (knowledge graphs as index, HippoRAG, A-Mem dynamic links, AriGraph, ChatDB, TiM tuples); (iii) timeline-based (chronological/causal sequences; Theanine, Zep bi-temporal valid/invalid timestamps); plus hierarchical tree structures (MemTree, ChatGPT-RSum recursive summary, hierarchical compression). So flat-vector, metadata-keyed, knowledge-GRAPH, timeline, and hierarchical/tree topologies are all surveyed.
retriever_type: Surveyed broadly: (i) lexical retrieval (TF-IDF, BM25, neural sparse models with learned query/doc expansion); (ii) semantic/dense retrieval (encode query+doc into vectors); (iii) commercial web search (Google/Bing APIs providing real-time, ranked, freshness-/authority-aware results); plus multimodal retrievers (CLIP/SigLIP/BLIP text-image similarity, LayoutLM/Donut layout-aware, ChartReader/Chartformer structure-aware). For memory, LLM-driven managers (Mem0, Memory-R1) and graph retrievers. Document selection/reranking uses cross-encoders, LLM-as-retriever (special True/relevance tokens), and reasoning rerankers (Rank-R1, ReasonRank). Hybrid fusion (RRF) is common.
retriever_learning_signal: Surveyed across the full range. Off-the-shelf (frozen BM25/dense). Contrastive similarity training (BGE point-wise embeddings). LM-feedback / distillation (RECOMP, Chain-of-Note summarizers trained on GPT-4 labels). Downstream-task-effectiveness / preference (BIDER optimized with PPO on answer-correctness gains; RankCoT via DPO; ReasonRank/Rank-R1 via GRPO on ranking reward). RL / learned policy is a central theme: Search-R1 frames retrieval as part of an MDP and uses RL to learn when+what to retrieve; R1-Searcher uses outcome rewards; Memory-R1 trains a Memory Manager via RL. So the survey traces a shift from similarity-only to LM-feedback, task-effectiveness/preference, and RL-trained retrieval/selection.
query_construction: Surveyed as query planning (Section 3.1): transforming a complex question into a structured sequence of executable sub-queries via (i) parallel planning (independent sub-queries resolved concurrently), (ii) sequential planning (linear, each step conditioned on intermediate outcomes; DRAGIN reformulates attention-selected tokens into focused queries; ReSP targets identified information gaps; LLatrieval generates a new question/pseudo-passage when verification fails), and (iii) tree-based planning (RAG-Star MCTS+UCT, DeepRAG binary-tree, DeepSieve/DTA DAG, MAO-ARAG orchestrated reformulation modules). So raw input, decomposed sub-queries, thought/attention-conditioned queries, and synthetic pseudo-passages are all surveyed.
query_granularity: Surveyed at multiple levels: task-level decomposition into sub-queries at planning time (parallel planning), trajectory/sequential-level (sequential planning where each sub-query depends on accumulated evidence; iterative QA), and step/state-level (per-step query reformulation conditioned on global+local memory state, e.g., ReSP, DRAGIN attention-driven; adaptive per-step retrieval). Tree-based planning constructs queries across branching decision nodes. So task-level, trajectory-level, and step/state-level query construction are all covered.
when_to_retrieve: Surveyed as 'retrieval timing' / adaptive retrieval (Section 3.2.2), tracing an evolution: fixed/per-step retrieval (IR-CoT retrieves after every reasoning step) -> dynamically triggered retrieval as a model-issued action (ReAct, Self-RAG, Search-o1) -> RL-trained retrieval policies (Search-R1 jointly optimizes when and what to retrieve). Modes covered: one-shot, iterative, active (uncertainty/knowledge-boundary triggered), and adaptive/learned-router. The survey lists retrieval timing as an open challenge (over- vs under-retrieval).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Surveyed as four adaptive-retrieval paradigms keyed to knowledge-boundary perception: (i) Probabilistic Strategy (trigger on low token-generation confidence; FLARE-style, DRAGIN); (ii) Consistency-based Strategy (Rowen triggers retrieval when cross-model/cross-lingual agreement is low); (iii) Internal-States Probing (CtrlA, UAR, SEAKR use the model's internal states as a faithful confidence signal); (iv) Verbalized Strategy (special action/reflection tokens: ReAct generates action text, Self-RAG emits a 'retrieve' token). Reasoning-driven timing (Search-o1 Reason-in-Documents) and RL-trained policies (Search-R1) are the recent frontier. Underpinned by confidence estimation: probabilistic, consistency-based, internal-state, and verbalized confidence.
reranking: Yes - a first-class topic under Information Filtering / Document Selection (Section 3.2.3). Surveyed reranking families: point-wise (cross-encoder binary relevance, BGE embedding similarity, LLM relevance tokens), pair-wise (PRP pairwise-ranking-prompting with heapsort and order-swap debiasing), and list-wise (RankGPT global ranking, TourRank tournament, ListT5 FiD-based parallel m-ary tournament, InstructRAG rationale-based, Rank-R1 and ReasonRank GRPO-trained reasoning rerankers). Multimodal results are fused via reciprocal-rank fusion (RRF) or cross-modal reranking.
retrieved_context_refinement: Surveyed extensively as Information Filtering with three approaches: (i) Document Selection (point/pair/list-wise reranking and top-k selection to drop noise); (ii) Context Compression - lexical-based (RECOMP summarization, Chain-of-Note reading notes, BIDER key supporting evidence, information-bottleneck noise filtering, RankCoT implicit-rerank-then-summarize) and embedding-based (ICAE, COCOM, xRAG single-token compression, ACC-RAG/QGC query-adaptive compression rates); (iii) Rule-based Cleaning (HtmlRAG removes HTML boilerplate). Motivated by LLM sensitivity to retrieval noise. So rerank, decompose/distill, distractor filtering, and compression are all covered.
how_retrieved_used: Surveyed across uses: prompt augmentation (feeding ranked/compressed evidence into the generator), latent-token injection (embedding-based compression projects documents into soft tokens, e.g., xRAG single token, ICAE/COCOM embedding sequences), training signal (SFT cold-start on distilled trajectories; end-to-end RL where retrieved tokens are masked in the policy-gradient loss, Search-R1), skill reuse (Voyager/GITM skill libraries), and case/experience reuse (episodic memory recall). In answer generation, retrieved evidence is integrated for grounded, citation-attributed synthesis (Self-RAG reflection-token-gated integration; Stateful Query Planning couples plan with evolving memory state, e.g., Plan-on-Graph, MCTS-OPS).
planning_integration: Surveyed as a dedicated component (Query Planning) tightly interleaved with retrieval/acting in a closed-loop research workflow. Integration patterns: parallel planning (decompose then retrieve in parallel), sequential/iterative plan-then-retrieve-then-replan (each sub-query conditioned on accumulated evidence; iterative QA, S3, AI-SearchPlanner decide when to stop), tree-search planning (RAG-Star MCTS+UCT with a retrieval-based reward and back-propagation; DeepRAG binary-tree; DeepSieve/DTA DAG aggregation), and end-to-end RL pipelines where planning, retrieval, tool use, and answer extraction are jointly optimized (Search-R1 as a fully observable MDP, R1-Searcher, Tool-Star/ARPO/AEPO). Multi-agent orchestration (Anthropic-style orchestrator + worker agents) coordinates planning, gathering, and synthesis.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Surveyed at several granularities: per-answer (one-shot retrieval before answering), per-CoT-step / per-reasoning-step (IR-CoT retrieves after every reasoning step; sequential planning re-queries per step on information gaps), per-token/per-sentence (probabilistic adaptive retrieval triggered by low-confidence tokens), and per-tool-call within a rollout (ReAct action text, Search-R1/Tool-Star multi-turn tool invocations in an RL rollout). MCTS-based planners interleave retrieval at each node expansion.
retrieved_item_representation: Surveyed surface forms: raw retrieved text/passages/web content; distilled/compressed summaries and reading notes (RECOMP, Chain-of-Note); latent/soft compressed embeddings (xRAG single token, ICAE/COCOM embedding sequences); structured notes / knowledge-graph triples and sub-graphs (HippoRAG, AriGraph, TiM tuples, ChatDB relational, Zep temporal KG); free-text workflows and skills (Voyager/GITM skill libraries, MIRIX procedural memory); and multimodal grounded pointers (table cells, chart coordinates) for citation. So raw text, distilled summaries, structured graphs/notes, executable skills, and latent-soft tokens are all surveyed.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Surveyed across abstraction levels: raw retrieved passages/web content (information acquisition); distilled summaries / event logs / high-level abstractions (unstructured memory consolidation: MemoryBank, MemoChat, ChatGPT-RSum, Generative Agents reflections); state-aware structured representations (knowledge graphs, trees - structured consolidation); reusable workflows / procedural skills (GITM common-reference memory, Voyager skill library, MIRIX procedural memory); and single demonstrations/notes. The memory component explicitly distills transient experiences into durable, higher-abstraction engrams.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Surveyed as a central concern: LLMs are highly sensitive to retrieval noise. Mechanisms covered: relevance evaluation / self-reflection (Self-RAG critic/reflection tokens; reasoning rerankers Rank-R1/ReasonRank/InstructRAG that judge document usefulness with rationales); reason-in-documents / reading-notes distillation (Search-o1 Reason-in-Documents, Chain-of-Note); information-bottleneck and KSE-based filtering (Zhu et al., BIDER); context compression to raise useful-content density; rule-based cleaning (HtmlRAG); and confidence/knowledge-boundary perception to avoid retrieving (or trusting) low-quality evidence. Consistency-based and internal-state probing further guard against unreliable context.
memory_type: Surveyed comprehensively as a distinct component (Memory Management): episodic (timestamped interaction histories), semantic (consolidated user traits/facts), graph (knowledge-graph memory: AriGraph, HippoRAG, Zep, ChatDB), tree/hierarchical (MemTree), skill-library/procedural (Voyager, GITM, MIRIX procedural memory), and parametric/latent (memory encoded in weights, modular memory). Distinguished from standard RAG by maintaining and revising a working memory across long horizons.
write_back: Yes (true) for the DR memory paradigm. The survey defines memory management with four core operations - Consolidation (transform short-term experiences into durable long-term representations), Indexing, Updating, and Forgetting - i.e., the agent actively writes back and maintains experiences/findings. Examples: MemGPT FIFO paging to long-term store, MemoryBank daily-event summaries, Mem0 ADD/UPDATE/DELETE, A-Mem dynamic linking. (Standard RAG, the contrast paradigm, does not write back.)
online_growth: Yes - the memory store grows and evolves during deployment/test-time. Memory consolidation converts ongoing interactions into durable memories, indexing creates new retrieval pathways, updating refines stored knowledge, and the store can prune via forgetting. A-Mem progressively grows a flexible access network; Generative Agents accumulate reflections; MEM1 maintains a constant-size evolving state. The survey contrasts this online-growing memory with RAG's frozen pre-indexed corpus.
write_back_trigger: Surveyed across triggers: per-step / use-and-discard (MEM1 synthesizes a compact state and discards raw context after each interaction; MemGPT FIFO eviction); reflective/after-self-critique (Generative Agents trigger reflection after sufficient event accumulation; Reflexion verbal self-correction; A-Mem Memory Evolution re-evaluates linked memories); on-success (GITM summarizes key actions from successful plans into reference memory; Voyager adds verified skills); and conflict-/contradiction-triggered (Mem0 UPDATE/DELETE, Zep edge-invalidation on superseding facts, TiM MERGE/FORGET). RL-trained managers (Memory-R1) learn when to ADD/UPDATE/DELETE.
failure_experience_usage: Surveyed mainly via self-reflection updating where agents reflect on past experiences (including failures) to refine knowledge (Reflexion verbal self-correction, Voyager skill-library updates, A-Mem memory evolution). The survey does not center an explicit success-vs-failure contrastive memory taxonomy; experiences are reactivated and modified based on new information or environmental feedback. Forgetting actively removes outdated/erroneous content (Mem0 DELETE, TiM FORGET, MEOW machine-unlearning of contradictory facts). So failure/correction signals are used chiefly through reflective updating and active forgetting rather than a dedicated negative-experience retrieval store.
memory_evolution_update: Surveyed in detail (Memory Updating + Forgetting). Update dynamics: integration & conflict resolution (Mem0 ADD/UPDATE, Zep effective-time-range modification, TiM MERGE), self-reflection reconsolidation (Reflexion, Voyager, A-Mem autonomous re-evaluation of linked memories), and parametric updating (global continued training, localized locate-and-edit, modular). Forgetting: passive decay (MemGPT FIFO, MemoryBank Ebbinghaus curve, MEM1 use-and-discard) and active removal (Mem0 DELETE, TiM FORGET, AriGraph vertex/edge removal, Zep non-destructive edge invalidation, MEOW unlearning). So append, dedup-merge, delta-update, refine-overwrite, forget-prune, and link-and-evolve are all surveyed.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Yes - a major surveyed axis. Retrieval/search is increasingly a learned/RL-optimized policy rather than fixed top-k: Search-R1 formulates search-augmented reasoning as a fully observable MDP and optimizes when+what to retrieve via RL (masking retrieved tokens in the policy-gradient loss); R1-Searcher learns search invocation via outcome rewards; Tool-Star/ARPO/AEPO optimize tool-use pipelines with GRPO. Reranking is also RL-learned (Rank-R1, ReasonRank GRPO). Memory management is cast as an RL decision problem (Memory-R1 Memory Manager; goal-driven reinforced memory evolution as a future direction with long-term credit-assignment challenge).
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Partially surveyed. The workflow-prompting paradigm centers multi-agent orchestration (e.g., Anthropic's orchestrator + parallel worker agents sharing an evidence ledger; multi-agent distillation with planner/tool-caller/verifier; Chain-of-Agents distilling multi-agent capability into one model; OAgents/OWL). Memory in these settings can be shared via a common evidence ledger / orchestrator. However, the survey does not foreground a dedicated cross-framework shared-memory taxonomy; most memory work surveyed is single-agent private memory, with multi-agent collaboration handled at the workflow/orchestration level.
benchmarks: Catalogs many benchmarks in Tables 4-5. Agentic information seeking / QA: Natural Questions (NQ), TriviaQA, SimpleQA, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, Bamboogle, MultiHop-RAG, FRAMES, GPQA, GAIA, HLE (Humanity's Last Exam), BrowseComp, BrowseComp-Plus. Interaction environments: InfoDeepSeek, AssistantBench, Mind2Web, Mind2Web 2, WebArena, WebWalkerQA, WideSearch, MMInA, DeepResearchBench, DeepResearchGym. Report generation: AutoSurvey, ReportBench, SurveyGen, Deep Research Comparator, DeepResearch Bench, ResearcherBench, LiveDRBench, PROXYQA, SCHOLARQABENCH. Poster/Slides: Paper2Poster, PosterGen, P2PInstruct, Doc2PPT, SLIDESBENCH, Zenodo10K, TSBench. AI-for-research: AI Idea Bench, Scientist-Bench, PaperBench, ASAP-Review.
benchmark_family: QA / multi-hop (NQ, TriviaQA, SimpleQA, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, Bamboogle, MultiHop-RAG, FRAMES); knowledge-intensive reasoning (GPQA, GAIA, HLE); web / live-browsing (Mind2Web, Mind2Web 2, WebArena, WebWalkerQA, BrowseComp, BrowseComp-Plus, InfoDeepSeek, AssistantBench, WideSearch, MMInA, DeepResearchBench, DeepResearchGym); long-form report & survey generation (AutoSurvey, ReportBench, SurveyGen, ResearcherBench, LiveDRBench, PROXYQA, SCHOLARQABENCH, Deep Research Comparator); presentation generation (Paper2Poster, PosterGen, Doc2PPT, SLIDESBENCH, Zenodo10K, TSBench); AI-for-research (AI Idea Bench, Scientist-Bench, PaperBench, ASAP-Review). Not the embodied (ALFWorld) or decision-RL (D4RL) families.
baselines: N/A (a survey, not a method - it runs no head-to-head experiments of its own and reports no baseline comparison table). Conceptually it positions standard RAG as the baseline against the three Deep Research stages (Agentic Search, Integrated Research, Full-stack AI Scientist) in Table 1, and compares optimization paradigms (workflow prompting vs SFT vs end-to-end RL) and data-synthesis approaches (strong-to-weak distillation vs multi-agent distillation vs iterative self-evolving) qualitatively. It cites representative systems (Search-R1, R1-Searcher, WebDancer, WebSailor, WebThinker, Chain-of-Agents, OpenAI/Gemini/Perplexity DeepResearch) as the landscape rather than running comparisons.
key_metrics: Surveys metrics rather than reporting its own (Tables 4-5). QA/seeking: Exact Match, F1, Accuracy, Recall, Recall@k, Step Success Rate, Action Count, Search Call, Calibration Error, Similarity. Web/agent: Correctness, Success Rate, Agent-as-a-Judge. Report/long-form: Citation Quality, Content Quality, key-point coverage, Report Relevance / Retrieval Faithfulness / Report Quality, Precision/Recall/F1, Rubric/Factual Assessment, Bradley-Terry score, LLM-as-Judge. Presentation: Visual Quality, Textual Coherence, ROUGE, BERTScore, layout/design scores. Phase I prioritizes retrieval recall@k + answer exact match + citation correctness + latency; Phase II shifts to fine-grained factuality, verified citations, structural coherence, and key-point coverage.
headline_result: N/A (no single experimental headline number - it is a survey). Its headline conceptual contributions are: (i) a three-stage capability roadmap distinguishing DR from RAG (Standard RAG -> Agentic Search -> Integrated Research -> Full-stack AI Scientist, Table 1); (ii) four foundational components each with fine-grained sub-taxonomies - Query Planning (parallel/sequential/tree-based), Information Acquisition (retrieval tools/timing/filtering), Memory Management (consolidation/indexing/updating/forgetting), Answer Generation (integration/synthesis/structuring/presentation); (iii) three optimization paradigms (workflow prompting, SFT, end-to-end agentic RL); and (iv) a consolidated evaluation landscape across information-seeking and long-form generation with 30+ benchmarks.
ablations: N/A (no experiments, hence no ablations). The analytical equivalents are comparative analyses: (1) capability comparison of Standard RAG vs the three DR stages across 11 feature axes (Table 1: search-engine access, tool use, code execution, reflection, memory management, hypothesis proposal, long-form generation, action space, reasoning horizon, workflow organization, output form); (2) output-capability comparison of contemporary DR systems (Table 2: text/image/audio/video/presentation/table/JSON/code/chart/GUI/citation across Gemini/OpenAI/Grok/H2O.ai/Skywork/Perplexity/Manus/Alita etc.); (3) comparison of single-agent vs multi-agent distillation vs iterative self-evolving data synthesis (Figure 7); (4) RL training-stability analyses (void-turn filtering / SimpleTIR, Echo-Trap / StarPO-S).
evaluation_decoupling: Yes - the survey frames evaluation as two complementary aspects: (i) evaluation of agentic information-seeking capabilities (intrinsic: retrieval recall@k, search call count, accuracy, EM) and (ii) evaluation of long-form generation (report quality, citation faithfulness, coherence). Several surveyed benchmarks report intrinsic retrieval/process metrics separately from end-to-end outcome (e.g., BrowseComp-Plus reports Accuracy/Recall/Search Call/Calibration Error; DeepResearchGym reports Report Relevance / Retrieval Faithfulness / Report Quality; InfoDeepSeek reports Accuracy/Utilization/Compactness). So intrinsic retrieval metrics are decoupled from end-task metrics in the surveyed landscape.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both, and the survey advocates process-aware evaluation. Outcome: EM/F1/Accuracy/Success Rate/Correctness for short-form and Content Quality/Rubric/LLM-Judge for long-form. Process: Step Success Rate, Action Count, Search Call count, Retrieval Faithfulness, citation correctness/verified citations, key-point coverage, calibration error, and logical-coherence assessment (proposed multi-granularity sentence/paragraph/document coherence). Section 6.4 raises logical evaluation, the novelty-vs-hallucination boundary, and LLM-as-Judge bias/efficiency as open process-evaluation challenges.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Discussed qualitatively and as a challenge. The survey repeatedly weighs retrieval/inference cost vs accuracy: adaptive retrieval is motivated by the cost/overhead of blind per-step retrieval (over-retrieval vs under-retrieval); context compression (xRAG single-token, ACC-RAG/QGC query-adaptive rates) cuts token/context cost; Chain-of-Agents reduces compute vs multi-agent systems while preserving accuracy; AEPO/ARPO improve rollout efficiency; multi-agent distillation incurs substantial inference cost and infrastructure overhead. Benchmark metrics include Search Call count, Action Count, end-to-end latency, and editing efficiency. LLM-as-Judge efficiency (cost of large-scale pairwise evaluation) is flagged as an open issue. No single quantitative headline cost number (it is a survey).
context_budget_and_selection_count: Surveyed budget levers: top-k document selection then reranking-then-truncation (Document Selection); context compression to fit/raise density within the LLM context window (lexical summarization and embedding-based, with query-adaptive compression rates in ACC-RAG/QGC); rule-based cleaning (HtmlRAG) to remove boilerplate; and memory forgetting / FIFO paging (MemGPT) plus use-and-discard constant-size state (MEM1) to cap working-memory budget. Anthropic-style orchestration allocates explicit budgets of agents, tool calls, and synthesis passes scaled to query complexity (1-2 agents for factual lookups up to more for complex queries). So budgets are fixed-k, query-adaptive/precision-driven, and budget-capped.
survey_scope_and_axes: Explicit organizing axes: (1) three-stage capability roadmap - Phase I Agentic Search, Phase II Integrated Research, Phase III Full-stack AI Scientist - vs Standard RAG (Table 1); (2) four foundational components, each with fine-grained sub-taxonomies: Query Planning (parallel / sequential / tree-based), Information Acquisition (retrieval tools [lexical/semantic/web/multimodal] / retrieval timing [adaptive: probabilistic/consistency/internal-state/verbalized] / information filtering [document selection / context compression / rule-based cleaning]), Memory Management (consolidation / indexing / updating / forgetting), Answer Generation (integrating upstream / synthesizing & coherence / structuring reasoning & narrative / presentation generation); (3) three optimization paradigms (workflow prompting, SFT [strong-to-weak / multi-agent distillation / iterative self-evolving], end-to-end agentic RL); (4) evaluation across information-seeking and long-form generation; (5) challenges (retrieval timing, memory evolution, training instability, evaluation) and open discussion (creativity, fairness, safety). Coverage: 8 sections, 30+ benchmarks tabulated, 500+ references; time window roughly 2019-2025 (v1 Nov 2025), with a continuously-updated companion repo.
builds_on: Synthesizes and builds conceptually on: standard RAG (Lewis et al.; surveyed as the static-corpus predecessor it distinguishes DR from); iterative/adaptive retrieval (IR-CoT, FLARE, Self-RAG, DRAGIN, Search-o1); agentic reasoning-acting (ReAct, WebGPT/SearchGPT); RL-trained search agents (Search-R1, R1-Searcher/++, Tool-Star, ARPO, AEPO); web agents (WebDancer, WebSailor, WebThinker, WebShaper, Chain-of-Agents); memory systems (MemGPT, MemoryBank, Generative Agents, Reflexion, Voyager, GITM, HippoRAG, A-Mem, Mem0, Zep, TiM, AriGraph, Memory-R1); planning/tree-search (RAG-Star MCTS, DeepRAG, DeepSieve); compression (RECOMP, Chain-of-Note, xRAG, ICAE/COCOM); and commercial DR systems (OpenAI/Gemini/Perplexity/Grok/Anthropic DeepResearch, Manus, Skywork, H2O.ai).
contrasts_with: Primarily positions Deep Research against conventional/standard RAG, arguing RAG operates in a static retrieval loop over pre-indexed corpora and treats retrieval as a heuristic augmentation step without a flexible research workflow or broad action space, whereas DR enables flexible interaction with the dynamic digital world, long-horizon autonomous planning, dynamic memory management, and verifiable long-form generation (Table 1; Section 2.3). Also contrasts with prior surveys that only cover RAG or web agents in isolation, with single-shot prompting / static parametric knowledge, and internally contrasts the three optimization paradigms and the single- vs multi-agent distillation vs iterative self-evolving data-synthesis approaches.
lineage: Surveys lineage. Positioned as a foundational, systematic survey of the Deep Research (DR) paradigm - the agentic, tool-augmented, long-horizon successor to RAG and web agents. It sits in the Surveys group alongside RAG surveys (Gao et al.), agentic-RAG surveys, agent/memory surveys, and context-engineering surveys, but uniquely consolidates the DR-specific workflow (query planning + information acquisition + memory management + answer generation) and its optimization (prompting/SFT/RL) and evaluation. It is upstream of and frequently cited by subsequent DR benchmark/method papers (e.g., Knowledgeable Deep Research, structural-evaluation work, FinDeepForecast).
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based-reasoning work; the survey does not organize DR around a Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain case cycle. Its memory-management loop - consolidation/indexing/updating/forgetting - is functionally adjacent but framed in cognitive-memory rather than CBR terms.)
explicit_cbr_grounding: false. The survey does not frame Deep Research as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it draws on cognitive-neuroscience memory analogies (consolidation, engrams, Ebbinghaus forgetting curve) rather than the CBR ontology.
tool_document_engineering: Partially surveyed under retrieval tools and multimodal retrieval rather than as explicit tool-description engineering. The survey discusses indexing/search techniques for retrieval tools (lexical inverted indices with learned query/doc term expansion, dense embeddings, commercial web-search ranking) and multimodal indexing of titles/captions/layout/chart schemas, but does not center a dedicated taxonomy of tool/skill docstring augmentation (synthetic-query expansion, weighted-field embeddings, instruction-tuned tool embeddings) the way tool-retrieval-specific papers do.
index_content_separation: Partially surveyed. Memory indexing is explicitly distinguished from memory consolidation: indexing builds a lightweight navigational map (vector embeddings, summaries, entity tags, LSH/HNSW/FAISS access structures) over already-consolidated heavier memory content - a lightweight-index-then-content pattern. Hierarchical/tree structures (MemTree, recursive summaries) and signal-enhanced metadata indices support searching a compact index before loading full content. Not framed explicitly as SOP-index-then-content progressive disclosure.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Partially surveyed. The survey emphasizes DR's shift from static, closed-corpus retrieval to live commercial web search (Google/Bing APIs) and real-time tool/web-API interaction with up-to-date information, and notes web-fetch / PDF-parsing / calculator tool registries (Anthropic-style central tool registry). Memory stores are live-synchronized via updating/forgetting (Mem0 ADD/UPDATE/DELETE, Zep bi-temporal). However, it does not provide a dedicated MCP / RapidAPI / function-calling protocol taxonomy with CRUD auto-sync the way tool-retrieval-specific papers do.
tool_dependency_awareness: Largely N/A as a focused axis. The survey covers tool use and multi-tool scenarios (Tool-Star, ARPO, AEPO, multi-agent tool callers) and graph-based memory of inter-entity relationships, but it does not center an explicit inter-tool dependency-modeling taxonomy (output-of-A-feeds-B, shared auth, prerequisite/dependency graphs, dependency-aware reranking) for tool retrieval.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A in the CBR sense (no verbatim-case adaptation/revision cycle). The functionally related mechanisms surveyed are self-reflection updating of memory (Reflexion verbal self-correction, A-Mem memory evolution, Voyager skill refinement), execution/environment-feedback-driven memory updates (Mem0, Memory-R1 RL manager), and answer-generation reconciliation of conflicting evidence (Self-RAG reflection tokens, Plan-on-Graph reflection-guided self-correction) - i.e., experience/memory revision rather than CBR case adaptation.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A as an authored benchmark (this is a survey, not a benchmark paper). It instead tabulates 30+ existing benchmarks with dates, aspects, data sizes, and metrics (Tables 4-5), e.g., HotpotQA (90124/5617/5813; EM/F1/Acc), 2WikiMultihopQA (167454/12576/12576), GPQA (448; Accuracy), GAIA (450/466; Exact Match), BrowseComp (1266; EM), BrowseComp-Plus (830; Accuracy/Recall/Search Call/Calibration Error), HLE (2500; EM/Accuracy), FRAMES (824), Mind2Web (2350), Mind2Web 2 (130; Agent-as-a-Judge), WebArena (812; Correctness), WebWalkerQA (680), WideSearch (200; LLM Judge), AutoSurvey (530000; Citation/Content Quality), SCHOLARQABENCH (2967), DeepResearchGym (96000). Construction methods span human-curated, multi-hop-composed (MuSiQue bottom-up), and closed academic (HLE - not answerable via quick online search), with difficulty signaled by low best-system scores on BrowseComp/HLE/GAIA.
